record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: In federated learning under poisoning and evasion attacks, how can defenses be evaluated against realistic adversary capabilities, including Byzantine clients, collusion, targeted backdoors, white-box model access, limited participation, and the distinction between data poisoning and model-update poisoning?

evidence.quote: many other characteristics of an adversary’s capabilities

artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad open research challenge highlighted as part of the federated-learning research agenda. Subsequent work (e.g., on Byzantine-robust aggregation, certified defenses against backdoors, and benchmarks such as those building on Krum, trimmed-mean, FLTrust, and backdoor evaluation suites) has made partial progress on individual axes (data vs. model poisoning, certified backdoor defenses), but no unified evaluation framework or defense covering all listed capabilities (collusion, white-box, limited participation, targeted backdoors, joint training/inference attacks) has been established. The problem remains open as a whole.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Lists adversary characteristics and evaluation of defenses as open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Problem posed as an open challenge in the federated learning research agenda.

status_evidence.title: Back to the Drawing Board: A Critical Evaluation of Poisoning Attacks on Production FL
status_evidence.snippet: Argues current evaluations of FL poisoning defenses use unrealistic threat models; calls for more realistic benchmarks.
status_evidence.claim: Realistic evaluation of FL defenses remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Federated Learning Poisoning Attacks and Defenses
status_evidence.snippet: Survey notes lack of unified framework covering data vs. model poisoning, collusion, and backdoor attacks.
status_evidence.claim: No comprehensive defense/evaluation framework exists across all adversary capabilities.
